resources.string: Follow one drive through a GPS jump, signal loss, and recovery. The app rejects the jump, estimates the position during the outage, then counts a route alert when the vehicle takes a side road.
The vehicle follows the planned road through the curve on the right. The green position marker should follow the road, with no route departure alert.
At 3 seconds, the red GPS cross jumps far away. The green position marker should stay at the last reliable spot until a valid reading arrives.
The vehicle is stopped. GPS reports inconsistent or missing heading, but the accepted position should stay in the same place.
Two GPS readings report poor accuracy. The app should keep the last reliable position until accurate readings return.
GPS reports arrive twice, out of order, or too late. The app should reject those readings and preserve the last reliable position.
GPS briefly drops out on a straight road. Watch the amber diamond estimate the position until enough reliable GPS readings arrive.
GPS stays unavailable in the tunnel. The amber estimate should give way to the last reliable position at 17 seconds. Later, the app should pick up GPS again.
The vehicle slows and stops while GPS is out. Compare the blue square (vehicle position) with the amber diamond (estimate), which keeps moving until GPS recovers.
GPS returns with gaps and poor readings. The app should hold the last reliable position or show an estimate until three reliable readings arrive in a row.
GPS places the vehicle between two parallel roads on the left. The app should show the observed position and leave the road unconfirmed.
The vehicle takes the side road in the middle of the map. Look for one route departure alert in Run results.
The vehicle stays on the planned road, but one GPS reading jumps toward the side road. The app should reject it. Look for zero route departure alerts in Run results.
The vehicle takes the side road and later rejoins the planned road. The route status should return to on route after three reliable readings on the planned road.
The only GPS reading has poor accuracy. The blue square still shows the simulated vehicle, and the app should display No fix throughout.
Try Pause to freeze the clock, Step to advance to the next event, and Reset to return to the start. Playback speed should leave the final results unchanged.
The vehicle takes the side road while GPS is out. A route departure alert should appear in the results only after GPS recovers and confirms the new road.
One GPS reading has a negative accuracy and another claims it was measured in the future. Both should be rejected while the last reliable position stays visible.
